mission: For each competitor in {Palantir Foundry Ontology, Neo4j, AWS Neptune, Stardog}, identify strengths, where Oyatie lacks, and measurable patches for specs/products/ontology.json.

source_policy.claim_rule: Competitor claims in this artifact must cite source_evidence ids; Oyatie target metrics are internal goals and must be bench-proven before launch.

source_evidence.claim: Palantir ontologies contain object types, link types, action types, interfaces, shared properties, and groups; they can be private or shared across organizations, with ontology-space mapping.

The Foundry Ontology is an operational/digital-twin layer with semantic elements, kinetic elements such as actions/functions/dynamic security, and backend services for datasource management, querying/searching/aggregating, and write orchestration.
A Foundry Action is a single transaction changing properties of one or more objects based on user-defined logic and can be triggered from applications or APIs.
Palantir object permissioning distinguishes ontology resources/schema from objects and links/data, with granular security controls over both levels.
Neo4j uses a property graph model with nodes, labels, directed typed relationships, and key-value properties on nodes/relationships.
Neo4j schema is optional, and indexes/constraints can be introduced for performance and modeling benefits.
Neo4j vector indexes retrieve neighborhoods by embedding similarity; explicit dimensions are recommended to fail mismatches clearly.
Neo4j vector search is approximate and has limitations such as transaction visibility behavior; it should not be treated as exact policy truth.
Neptune supports Gremlin, openCypher, and SPARQL; Gremlin/openCypher query property graph data, while SPARQL queries RDF.
Neptune Analytics exposes optimized openCypher procedures for graph algorithms across pathfinding, centrality, similarity, community detection, vector similarity, and graph summary/statistics.
Neptune Analytics vector index updates are not ACID atomic/isolated, so vector results must not be used as authoritative policy mutation truth without receipts.
Stardog Virtual Graphs declaratively map remote structured/semi-structured data into a knowledge graph and verify data source configuration/mappings when registered.
Stardog supports many data source categories for virtual graphs, including relational databases, NoSQL databases, SPARQL services, files/unstructured data, cloud services, and CRM.
Stardog supports query-time reasoning/inference over explicit data using schemas with RDFS/OWL axioms and user-defined rules, without materializing inferences.
Stardog virtual graphs require resource permissions and named graph security for sensitive virtual data; passthrough authentication can limit virtual graph access to backing datasource permissions.

where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: ontology PRD has semantic/kinetic/dynamic layers but lacks explicit object-action transaction receipts
shared/private ontology-space model is not encoded
permission model does not explicitly separate schema resources from object/link data
materialized latest-state/export path is not first-class

measurable_patches.patch: Add object_action_transaction_receipt for every create/update/delete/link mutation.
measurable_patches.measure: each action emits action_id, object_ids, link_ids, rule_id, idempotency_key, actor_principal, permission_decision_ref, audit_chain_ref

measurable_patches.patch: Add ontology_space_partition model for private/shared ontology projections.
measurable_patches.measure: schema distinguishes tenant_private, org_shared, and public_projection spaces with explicit allowed_org_marks

measurable_patches.patch: Split permission checks into ontology_resource and object_link_data tiers.
measurable_patches.measure: Cedar policy coverage proves both tiers evaluated before action execution

reject_or_constrain: Do not copy Palantir closed-platform assumptions or unsourced single-tenant claims; Oyatie stays open-spec and multi-tenant by design.

observed_strengths: schema-optional modeling with indexes/constraints when needed
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: ontology PRD lacks graph-query ergonomics acceptance tests
constraint/index declarations are not tied to ontology type registration
vector/semantic retrieval is not explicitly bounded away from policy truth
no source-backed stance on approximate vector limitations

measurable_patches.patch: Add graph_query_projection adapter for Cypher-like traversal/read APIs without making Neo4j a runtime dependency.
measurable_patches.measure: read-side traversal tests cover node-label, typed-edge, property-filter, shortest-path, and explain-plan receipt

measurable_patches.patch: Require index_constraint_plan per ontology type/link registration.
measurable_patches.measure: every queryable property/link has explicit index/constraint status or no_index_reason

measurable_patches.patch: Forbid approximate vector search as authorization or mutation truth.
measurable_patches.measure: policy/action gates reject vector_score_only decisions; require deterministic entity_id + permission proof

reject_or_constrain: Do not adopt an external Neo4j runtime dependency; keep Postgres/RLS + Oyatie ontology kernel as authority.

observed_strengths: vector similarity/search for GraphRAG use cases
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: ontology PRD lacks RDF/SPARQL/openCypher interoperability adapters
graph analytics algorithms are not specified as read-only/derived evidence lanes
vector index atomicity/consistency limitations are not reflected in anti-patterns
AWS-only service dependency conflicts with multi-cloud/on-prem requirement if adopted as authority

measurable_patches.patch: Add rdf_sparql_opencypher_interop adapters for import/export/query projection.
measurable_patches.measure: roundtrip fixtures preserve entity_id, edge_type, data_class, tenant_id, and audit provenance across RDF and property graph projections

measurable_patches.patch: Model graph algorithms as read-only derived evidence with freshness and reproducibility receipts.
measurable_patches.measure: algorithm result has source_snapshot_digest, algorithm_id, params, generated_at, and cannot directly mutate canonical graph

measurable_patches.patch: Forbid non-atomic vector-index updates from driving policy or canonical mutations.
measurable_patches.measure: mutation gate rejects vector-only evidence without canonical row/action receipt

reject_or_constrain: Do not make AWS Neptune required infrastructure; it can inform interop/analytics adapters only.

observed_strengths: SPARQL query rewriting to native source syntax
virtual graph security and passthrough authentication concepts
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: ontology PRD lacks virtual-source mapping receipts for existing enterprise systems
reasoning/rule layer is not separated from canonical typed actions
pass-through identity/security requirements are not explicit for adapter reads

measurable_patches.patch: Add virtual_source_mapping_receipt for every adapter-mapped external data source.
measurable_patches.measure: mapping receipt includes source_kind, schema_digest, mapping_digest, owner, credential_mode, data_class, freshness_budget, materialize_or_virtualize decision

measurable_patches.patch: Add reasoning_rule_tier separating inferred read projections from canonical writes.
measurable_patches.measure: inferred edges have inference_rule_id + source_snapshot_digest and cannot satisfy mutation/audit obligations without canonical evidence

measurable_patches.patch: Forbid virtual graph access without pass-through identity or named-graph-equivalent security.
measurable_patches.measure: adapter registration fails without credential_mode and named_scope_policy

reject_or_constrain: Do not adopt Stardog as external graph DB dependency; use as source pattern for adapters/reasoning only.

cross_competitor_patch_backlog: Add source-backed ontology competitive_claim schema: competitor, evidence_refs, observed_strengths, oyatie_gap, patch_id, verification.
Add ontology action transaction receipts covering object/link/create/update/delete mutations.
Add interop adapters for RDF/SPARQL/openCypher/property-graph projections without changing canonical storage authority.
Add deterministic separation between retrieval/vector/reasoning outputs and policy or mutation truth.
Add virtual-source mapping receipts and pass-through/named-scope security checks for enterprise data-source adapters.

changes: competitive entries for Palantir, Neo4j, Neptune, and Stardog rewritten with source_evidence_refs, observed strengths, gaps, and measurable patch backlog
best practices extended for source-backed competitor claims, action receipts, interop adapters, deterministic retrieval/reasoning boundaries, and virtual-source security
patterns extended for object actions, space partitions, query projections, interop adapters, graph analytics receipts, and virtual mappings
anti-patterns extended for unsourced benchmarks, external graph authority, vector/reasoning policy truth, and unsecured virtual graphs
